newsitem.title: GERMANY: Versace case houseboat owner may be German suspect.
newsitem.headline: Versace case houseboat owner may be German suspect.

text.p: German police said on Thursday they believed the owner of a houseboat where fashion designer Gianni Versace's alleged killer was found dead may be a fugitive they have been seeking since 1992.

A spokesman for police in the eastern city of Leipzig said they had been looking for Torsten Reineck, a man named in U.S. media reports as the owner of the houseboat where police found Andrew Cunanan dead in an apparent suicide on Wednesday.

The spokesman said Reineck was wanted on charges of fraud and tax evasion over two Leipzig businesses he set up. The companies, a marketing firm and a real estate company, later went bankrupt, the spokesman added.
He said a European arrest warrant had been issued for Reineck on those charges.
Asked if police believed the houseboat owner was the same man as the one they were looking for, the spokesman said: "It's speculative but we assume so. It would fit."

Versace was shot and killed on July 15 at the gate of his oceanfront mansion in the South Beach area of Miami Beach, about two miles (3 km) south of the houseboat's mooring. Cunanan was the prime suspect in the police investigation.
